Tell me how MangoDB persists writes to disk.

MangoDB persists writes to disk using a mechanism called **WAL (Write-Ahead Log)**. The WAL is a sequential file that records all changes to the database before they are written to the main data file. This ensures that even in the event of a system crash, the database can recover the most recent transactions.

When a write operation occurs in MangoDB, the system first writes the transaction to the WAL. This log entry includes the type of operation (e.g., insert, update, delete) and the specific data involved. Once the transaction is successfully recorded in the WAL, the actual data is written to the main data file. This process ensures data consistency and durability.

The WAL is crucial for recovery. If a crash occurs, the database can read the WAL to reconstruct the state of the database. This mechanism also helps in preventing data loss by ensuring that all transactions are recorded before they are applied to the database.

In summary, MangoDB uses the WAL to persist writes to disk, ensuring data integrity and recovery capabilities.
